lines.speaker: Agamemnon
lines.text: If you lost your mind, Ajax, and killed yourself, you nearly wiped out all of us too. Why are you still blaming Odysseus? Just the other day, when he came to ask the oracle, you wouldn't even look at him or say hello to your old comrade. You just strode past with your head held high.

lines.speaker: Ajax
lines.text: With good reason, Agamemnon. He caused my madness single-handedly by being set against me for the armor.

lines.speaker: Agamemnon
lines.text: Did you really think you were untouchable and should win without lifting a finger?

lines.speaker: Ajax
lines.text: Yes, for things like that. That armor was mine—it belonged to my cousin. The rest of you, who were much better than him, all gave up the contest and stepped aside for me. But Laertes' boy, the one I saved time and time again from getting chopped up by the Trojans, decides he's better and more fit to have the arms.

lines.speaker: Agamemnon
lines.text: Then you should blame Thetis, my friend. She was supposed to give you the arms as next of kin, but she threw them into the public pot instead.

lines.speaker: Ajax
lines.text: No, blame Odysseus. He's the one who challenged me.

lines.speaker: Agamemnon
lines.text: Give him a break, Ajax. He was just a man who wanted glory—the best thing there is, the thing we all risked everything for. And he did beat you, with the Trojans judging, no less.

lines.speaker: Ajax
lines.text: I know who passed sentence on me. But we can't speak against the gods. As for Odysseus, I couldn't stop hating him if I tried, Agamemnon—not even if Athena ordered me to.
